thread:
maria: thinking out loud — proposal to introduce a lightweight controlplane-bridge adapter that lives in a small ephemeral subnet inside customer VPCs. Purpose: fewer private endpoints, simpler routing for cert rotation/health checks, and reduced peering surface.

ajay: curious on the threat model first. ephemeral subnet still has outbound to our CP, right? how do we limit blast radius?

maria: yep. outbound-only via strict SG + egress-only NACL. adapter only initiates mTLS to CP, short lived IP leases, and pod runs with minimal IAM.

lin: what about route table churn for customers? adding subnets at scale makes ops tricky. any plan to avoid touching RTs?

maria: design idea: use a delegated subnet range we ask customers to pre-allocate (or we suggest a /28). then the adapter uses ENIs in that range. no route changes required for most setups.

ajay: hmm, customers will balk at allocating IPs. alternative: use existing private endpoint approach (privatelink) — less invasive but more costly per-customer. tradeoffs?

maria: exactly — privatelink = simpler for customers but we manage many endpoints and NATs. bridge adapter reduces endpoint count but increases customer config ask. cost vs operational surface tradeoff.

sara: also need to consider DNS and cert flow. if adapter is outbound mTLS, CP can't initiate cert rotation easily. do we flip to pull-based rotation?

maria: plan is push/pull hybrid: adapter periodically polls cert bucket and rotates on detection. CP can push a short-lived rotation token to adapter via existing control channel.

tomas: what about network path validation and monitoring? we lose some observability when we stop terminating at our private endpoints.

lin: good point. adapter should emit connection telemetry to our logs and add synthetic healthchecks. we can also preserve TCP/TLS handshake traces with sampling.

ajay: SCALING question: if many adapters burst (eg. onboarding), will CP see a conn storm? need backoff/queueing.

maria: yes — CP will need a token bucket and ephemeral session limit per-account. design includes staggered onboarding and exponential backoff in agent.

sara: ops playbook? if adapter breaks (bad SG or customer blocks egress) we need clear rollback without deleting customer resources.

maria: fallback = re-enable per-customer privatelink for a short window (automated), alert SE, and keep adapter in degraded mode. no deletions by default.

ajay: security review notes: 1) least privilege for adapter instance role, 2) enforce mTLS with client cert from HSM, 3) restrict metadata API access.

maria: agreed. we'll ban IMDSv1 and use instance profile proxies + sigv4 expiring creds.

lin: edge case: cross-account peering customers with strict subnet quotas — adapter might not fit. we need an opt-out path to keep existing peering model.

maria: yes opt-in by default for new customers; opt-out for customers who require traditional peering or privatelink. migration tooling will allow canary rollouts.

devops-bot: deployment checklist created: https://internal/infra/bridge-adapter/checklist — includes tests for egress policies, token-scaling, and cert rotation. :white_check_mark:

ajay: can we show a snippet for how adapter picks subnet? small pseudo-config would help prod team.

maria: sure — rough idea:
```
adapter:
  preferred_subnet: "10.64.2.0/28"
  lease_ttl: "30m"
  egress_targets:
    - cp.redwood.internal:443
    - s3.redwood-artifacts:443
```

sara: migration plan sketch: 1) small alpha customers opt-in, 2) enable observability for those accounts, 3) fail open to privatelink if adapter fails, 4) iterate on SG/NACL template.

lin: performance: will adapter add latency? small cpu-bound crypto, but SSD KV cache local to adapter can reduce overall CP RTT for repeated handshakes.

maria: benchmark expectations: +5–15ms median for first connection, net reduction in API hops for cert checks. we'll run a spike to validate.

ajay: last: billing/contract implications. if we reduce endpoints, infra cost moves from our account to customer (IP usage). need legal/finance sign-off.

maria: noted — will loop in finance.

tomas: I'll champion the security checklist in the next review. todo: write threat model doc and high-level sequence diagram.

maria: thanks all — action items: lin + ajay to draft ops fallback playbook, tomas + sara for sec/cert flow, i'll put up an RFC with sequence diagrams and rollout plan by EOW. :thumbsup:

ajay: ack.

lin: ack.

sara: ack.

maria: filing RFC link when ready.
